policy.acceptanceText: If you do not agree to this agreement, the submission policy, or maintainer review requirements, do not submit an app. If an accepted app later violates this agreement, maintainers may request changes, flag risk, delist, block, or retain audit records. The agreement may evolve with the project; material changes should be recorded publicly in the repository.
policy.agreementLead: This agreement applies to browsing, downloading, submitting, maintaining, or reviewing CardputerZero AppStore Hub apps, metadata, screenshots, binaries, and related discussions. Submitting an app means you have read and agree to these rules.
policy.agreementTitle: AppStore Hub User and Developer Agreement
device: Apps touching system settings, storage, network, sensors, or external modules must declare risk.
Apps must launch from APPLaunch and provide a clear exit path.
High CPU, storage, battery, or hardware risk must be visible on the detail page.
policy.lead: AppStore Hub puts user, device, maintainer, and open-source community trust first. Before submitting an app, developers must read and accept this agreement, privacy requirements, device-safety requirements, and rejection rules.
privacy: Apps must declare whether they collect, store, upload, or share user data.
Network, account, filesystem, and device identifier access must explain purpose.
Data collection should follow data minimization.
reject: Malware, credential theft, unauthorized persistence, or unauthorized access.
Hidden high-risk device behavior or undisclosed user-data collection.
Illegal, infringing, fraudulent, hateful, harassing, or harmful use.

sections.title: 1. Scope
items: This agreement covers app metadata, source code, binaries, icons, screenshots, README files, pull requests, issues, and comments submitted to the registry.
The Hub is a public directory and registry. It does not mean maintainers have performed a complete security audit for every app.
Before installing, users should review permissions, privacy, risk flags, source openness, download URLs, and checksums.

sections.title: 2. Developer responsibility
items: Developers must submit with a traceable GitHub identity and have the right to distribute all submitted code, assets, and binaries.
Developers must provide accurate, complete descriptions that do not mislead users or maintainers.
If download URLs, releases, source repositories, licenses, or app behavior changes, metadata should be updated promptly.

sections.title: 3. Metadata truthfulness
items: Network, filesystem, microphone, camera, sensors, GPS, external hardware, background service, and HDMI capabilities must be declared.
Source openness, license, commercial restrictions, version, checksum, dependencies, and device compatibility must be declared.
Paid limits, cloud services, account dependencies, high CPU, high storage, battery impact, or behavior that may damage user data must not be hidden.

sections.title: 4. Privacy and data
items: Apps that access, store, upload, or process user data must explain data type, purpose, retention, and third-party sharing.
Apps should follow data minimization and avoid collecting data unrelated to the feature.
If app behavior changes in a later version, the privacy declaration must be updated before or during release.

sections.title: 5. Device safety and UX
items: Apps must not intentionally damage the device, system files, user data, or external hardware.
GUI apps should fit the CardputerZero 320 x 170 screen and launch and exit correctly from APPLaunch.
Experimental, unfinished, special-setup, or device-risk apps must be clearly marked.

sections.title: 6. Prohibited content
items: Malware, spyware, credential theft, unauthorized persistence, unauthorized access, or review-bypass behavior is prohibited.
Illegal, infringing, fraudulent, phishing, impersonation, hateful, harassing, stalking, surveillance, weaponized, or harmful use is prohibited.
Hidden high-risk behavior, hidden commercial restrictions, unauthorized assets, or misleading install prompts are prohibited.

sections.title: 7. Review, listing, and delisting
items: Passing CI does not mean automatic listing; maintainers may request changes, additional declarations, demos, reproducible builds, or test logs.
Maintainers may mark apps as pending, ci-passed, approved, needs-changes, rejected, deprecated, or blocked.
Apps with clear user, device, legal, privacy, or community risk may be rejected, hidden, delisted, or blocked.

sections.title: 8. Appeals and records
items: Developers may appeal rejection, delisting, or blocked decisions through an issue or pull request.
Appeals should include app UUID, title, requested decision change, remediation notes, and evidence.
Maintainers should record final decisions where practical and may retain audit records without continuing to show install entries.

submit.agreementTitle: Read the agreement and admission rules first
ci: CI validates UUID, share code, required fields, icons, screenshots, download URL, and checksum.
When source is provided, CI may run source availability checks, basic static checks, dependency checks, builds, and smoke tests.
Passing CI does not mean automatic listing; maintainers still review policy, risk, and user experience.

submit.flowLead: Publish your app code or release in your own GitHub repository first, then submit metadata to the AppStore Hub registry repository.
submit.formatLead: App metadata uses YAML. GitHub Actions validates the file and generates registry.json, registry.yml, and the light index after merge.
submit.lead: Developers submit app metadata through GitHub pull requests. After maintainer approval, GitHub Actions generates a static registry and GitHub Pages publishes it to the Hub.
metadata: Every app needs a stable UUID. The share code defaults to the first four UUID characters and must be unique in the registry.
Title, summary, GitHub author, version, license, source openness, Debian .deb download URL, package name, and MD5 checksum are required.
Permissions, privacy behavior, external hardware, background service, HDMI, commercial restrictions, and known risks must be declared.
submit.metadataExample:
schema_version: 1
uuid: "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
title: "My Cardputer App"
summary: "One sentence user-facing summary."
description: "Longer description for the detail page."
categories:
  - Utilities
device_targets:
  - CardputerZero
author:
  github: "your-github-id"
version: "1.0.0"
license: "MIT"
source:
  openness: "open-source"
  repository: "https://github.com/your-github-id/my-cardputer-app"
download:
  type: "deb"
  package: "my-cardputer-app"
  url: "https://github.com/your-github-id/my-cardputer-app/raw/main/dist/my-cardputer-app_1.0.0_arm64.deb"
  md5: "..."
permissions:
  network: false
  microphone: false
  filesystem: "app-data-only"
privacy:
  collects_personal_data: false
  data_retention: "none"
assets:
  icon: "assets/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000/icon.png"
  screenshots:
    - "assets/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000/screenshots/main.png"
review:
  status: "pending"
review: In the pull request description, explain the app purpose, test method, download source, and whether it has been validated on CardputerZero.
Closed-source, binary-only, network, microphone, filesystem, external hardware, and background-service apps receive stricter review.
Maintainers may request changes, extra declarations, experimental labeling, rejection, delisting, or blocking; appeals are recorded in issues or pull requests.

steps.title: Prepare your app repository
steps.body: Commit your app code to GitHub and provide a clear README, license, build instructions, and release artifact. The download URL should be stable.

steps.title: Fork the registry repository
steps.body: Fork the CardputerZero/appstore-hub repository to your GitHub account and create a branch from the main branch for your submission.

steps.title: Add app metadata and assets
steps.body: Add a YAML metadata file named by UUID under apps/; place icon.png and screenshots under assets/<uuid>/.

steps.title: Fill metadata
steps.body: Complete title, summary, author, version, license, source, download, checksum, permissions, privacy, and risk fields according to the schema.

steps.title: Open a pull request
steps.body: Push your branch to your fork and open a pull request against AppStore Hub. Describe the app, test results, and any risks maintainers should review.

steps.title: Wait for CI and review
steps.body: GitHub Actions runs automatic checks first. After maintainer approval and merge, the Hub regenerates the static registry and publishes it to GitHub Pages.

submit.structureLead: The first registry version uses one YAML file per app. Display assets live in the matching UUID asset directory.

tutorial.title: Development And Submission Tutorial
tutorial.lead: A practical path from local app development, Debian packaging, and device validation to registry metadata, CI checks, and maintainer review.
tutorial.agreementTitle: Read The Agreement And Admission Rules First
tutorial.agreementLead: Opening a pull request confirms that metadata is truthful, permissions are complete, downloads are verifiable, and you will cooperate with maintainer review. Full rules now live in Documents.
tutorial.flowLead: The left lane is the developer preparation flow. The right lane is registry automation and maintainer review. Each major step links to Markdown documentation.

devFlow.title: Build the app
devFlow.body: Keep source, README, license, build steps, and release history in your own GitHub repository.

devFlow.title: Package .deb
devFlow.body: Use APPLaunch-compatible paths and produce a Debian package installable on Raspberry Pi OS.

devFlow.title: Validate on device
devFlow.body: Check icon, launch, exit, permissions, peripherals, and framebuffer behavior on CardputerZero.

devFlow.title: Prepare metadata
devFlow.body: Fill UUID, share code, author, version, download URL, MD5, permissions, privacy, and risk statements.

devFlow.title: Open a PR
devFlow.body: Fork the registry repository, add app YAML and assets, then open a pull request.

reviewFlow.title: Automated checks
reviewFlow.body: GitHub Actions validates fields, UUIDs, share codes, assets, download URLs, checksums, and registry generation.

reviewFlow.title: Risk review
reviewFlow.body: Maintainers review source availability, sensitive permissions, services, hardware, privacy, and device safety.

reviewFlow.title: Change requests
reviewFlow.body: If declarations are incomplete or risks are unclear, maintainers request metadata, package, or test updates.

reviewFlow.title: Merge and publish
reviewFlow.body: Approved PRs regenerate JSON/YAML registries and publish through GitHub Pages.

reviewFlow.title: Maintain updates
reviewFlow.body: Update registry metadata when downloads, versions, permissions, or behavior changes.
